November 18, 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted U.S. President Donald Trump on the tarmac at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport—breaking a roughly 50-year diplomatic norm in which Chinese vice presidents or senior officials typically handle airport arrivals.  • Breaking decades of protocol. Chinese paramount leaders rarely—if ever—appear at an airport to greet visiting foreign heads of state, typically delegating that role to a vice president or senior Communist Party official. During Trump’s visit to Beijing in May 2026, he was met by Vice President Han Zheng. • Reciprocating Trump’s earlier gesture. Chinese state news agency Xinhua noted that Xi’s personal welcome returned the goodwill Trump showed in September 2026, when Trump broke U.S. norms to personally greet Xi and his wife at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington. Xi stated on the tarmac that China values "reciprocating goodwill." • Signaling diplomatic hierarchy. In Beijing, the rank of the official sent to the airport reflects China's diplomatic pecking order. Earlier the same day in Shenzhen, Russian President Vladimir Putin was greeted by Xi’s chief of staff, Cai Qi, while Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was met by a foreign ministry protocol official—placing Trump's reception visibly above other visiting leaders. #trump #usa #china #politics #breakingnews
